notes: HVS17 is the sole eligible star. It is recorded as follow_up because T:p2-b2 identifies it as a newly discovered HVS from Brown et al. (2012b) and describes this paper’s Keck spectroscopy of it; T:p4-b2 explicitly retains the unbound candidacy by describing it as traveling at an unbound radial velocity.

HVS17: The paper does not report explicit numerical right ascension or declination; the SDSS identifier was not converted into coordinates. The +445 km/s value is described as a Galactic-rest-frame radial velocity and is excluded from radial_velocity under the stated rules; no total three-dimensional Galactic-rest-frame speed is reported. The proper-motion values in T:p5-b3 are model predictions for two origin scenarios, not measured astrometry. The rounded 50 kpc distance mentioned in the introduction/title is not recorded separately because the measured heliocentric distance is 49.6 ± 4.6 kpc; the 48.5 ± 4.6 kpc value is Galactocentric.
